the iron, nickel and copper salts of the carboxylic acids, phenols and hydroquinone, and the salts of certain other phenols, can be chromatographed with a high degree of similarity to the corresponding phenols and hydroxyquinone.

iron, nickel, cobalt, and other transition-metal salts can be mistaken for phenols by paper chromatography; the salts can be differentiated from phenols by their lack of colour reactions with the spray reagents, by their spectra, and by their different RF values.

the identification and characterization of the organic components of the Orgueil and Murchison meteorites, and with the determination of their relative abundance.
